E040-01.notes: Redundancy: 'before he could draw them, so he could never finish a sketch' says the same thing twice; B repeats it with a vague 'which meant'; D is awkwardly ordered and still redundant. C is concise and complete.

flags: minor: tests the same nonrestrictive comma+which point as E040-11
E040-02.notes: There is one specific camera, so a nonrestrictive comma + which is right. Without the comma (B), the clause turns restrictive, which is wrong here. C and D create a semicolon error and a fragment.

E040-03.notes: Dangling modifier: the person 'working outdoors' must be the subject, so 'he' follows. A, B and C all dangle.

flags: minor: A is grammatical and only mildly wordy ('and also moved it carefully'); it is wrong only on concision, which is the standard ACT basis
E040-04.notes: 'with a feather and a thin wooden splint, tools that would not melt the ice' is concise. C has redundant 'as well as additionally' and D has 'too' plus 'both being some tools'.

E040-05.notes: The comma after 'time' must pair with an opening comma before 'who'. B leaves a lone comma between the subject and the verb 'laughed'. C uses 'whom' where the subject form is needed. D's semicolon is wrong.

E040-06.notes: An interrupting 'however' needs commas on both sides. C adds a comma between the verb and its object. D's semicolon is wrong.

flags: minor: factual nuance - feathery dendrites depend mainly on high humidity at about -15 C, and are not simply favored by 'warmer' air (the warmest growth range, around -2 C, gives plates)
E040-07.notes: The new sentence gives an example of the weather-to-shape link named in sentence 12. B is not a real contradiction. A and D misdescribe the sentence.

E040-09.notes: The subject 'collection' is singular, so 'was' (past tense fits 'soon used'). 'Photographs' and 'pages' are distractors.

E040-10.notes: Only B goes back to the farm where he first studied snowflakes, which is the opening. A points to the shed in paragraph 2. C and D drift off topic and would not set up sentence 17 about the negatives.

E040-11.notes: The clause adds information about all the negatives just mentioned, so it is nonrestrictive and takes a comma + which. B gives a semicolon error and D a fragment.
